CityView: Implementation Specialist / Business Analyst

Reporting to the Manager of Professional Services, the successful individual will work closely with customers to understand their business requirements, configure the CityView software solution to meet those requirements and deliver training to those clients to ensure value creation. This is a fully remote position; however, travel to client sites across the U.S. and Canada may be required.

What’s Your Impact:

  • Delivering software solutions that help clients improve efficiency and service delivery.
  • Streamlining workflows to help optimize client processes and responsiveness.
  • Supporting local governments in enhancing services for their communities.

What You’ll Do:

  • Business analysis: Define and document customer business requirements; interpret and apply the information within project scope.
  • Process mapping: Analyze client requirements and translate them into functional specifications aligned with CityView-defined processes.
  • Gap analysis: Identify gaps between client needs and out-of-the-box system capabilities.
  • Discovery: Facilitate discovery sessions to document business requirements, use cases, and pain points.
  • Software configuration: Configure workflows, business rules, and system settings to support and streamline customer business processes. This role focuses on software configuration and business process enablement rather than software development.
  • Legacy data conversion: Work with Data Conversion Specialists to achieve a smooth transition of legacy client data.
  • Conduct training sessions: Train end-users in how to use the software in both remote and classroom-led sessions.
  • Software specialist: Develop expertise in CityView functionality and capabilities to support clients and identify enhancement opportunities.
  • Client service: Provide exceptional customer service and support clients throughout the implementation lifecycle.
  • Internal engagement: Work with cross-functional teams including Project Managers, Data Conversion Specialists, Quality Assurance, Technical Support Analysts, and other Implementation Specialists.

A Day In The Life:

  • Receive project assignments and priorities from the Project Manager.
  • Work on assigned tasks:
    • Engage with clients.
    • Gather and validate client data requirements.
    • Configure, test, and validate software solutions.
    • Deliver solutions to clients.
    • Action client feedback.
    • Provide project status updates and maintain internal tracking systems.

What We’re Looking For:

  • A highly focused and accountable individual.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively in a changing environment.
  • Experience and/or knowledge of local government business processes.
  • 5+ years of experience with software configuration, business process analysis, and/or end-user training is preferred.
  • Experience identifying, defining, analyzing, and documenting client work processes, data, systems, and/or related activities.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with experience in business analysis.
  • Understanding of licensing, permitting, or related government business processes (or equivalent).
  • Post-secondary education in a technology-related discipline or equivalent work experience.
  • Outstanding verbal and written communication skills in a highly professional, customer-facing environment.
  • Ability to travel up to 15% in Canada and the US.

What Makes You Stand Out:

  • Experience with permitting, licensing, land management, or related government processes.
  • An understanding of database (installed and web-based) applications.
  • Experience with MS SQL Reporting Services (or equivalent).

What We Offer:

  • RRSP matching program and employee stock purchase plan.
  • Health insurance from Day 1 (medical, dental, vision, life, short and long-term disability, AD&D).
  • 3 weeks of vacation and 5 personal days.

Who We Are:

CityView solves real-world business problems that local governments face in serving their constituents expeditiously. We do this by streamlining the complex business processes of permit, license and land management applications and approvals by providing constituents with online self-service tools and government employees with software that improves operational efficiency. We seek individuals with long-term career goals who thrive in a growing and evolving environment. We also seek people who embrace change and can prosper in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

Salary range: $65,000 - $75,000 CAD per year.

We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.

We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. Job Description

Olsson provides multidisciplinary, preliminary, and construction design services for mixed-use, commercial, and residential land development projects, along with industrial, sports, schools, and other site development types. As a Civil Project Engineer in either our Dallas or Fort Worth office, you will apply diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices to a broad variety of assignments and related fields. The project engineer is a registered professional engineer, whose supervision and guidance relate largely to overall objectives, critical issues, new concepts, and policy matters. The project engineer supervises, coordinates, and reviews work of engineers or technicians and performs complex or novel assignments that require development of new and improved techniques and procedures.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Prepares planning and design documents in appropriate engineering discipline.
  • Performs process design calculations, prepares cost estimates, and uses economic analyses for comparison of alternatives.
  • Assists with or develops project scope of work or portions of it; assists with or develops project schedule or portions of it; assists with completion of initiation paperwork; assists with budget reviews and schedules progress reports.
  • Coordinates projects with other Olsson teams; performs and coordinates design aspects of projects; directs team members on design tasks; maintains project records (correspondence, drawings, and files); informs project managers of progress and problems; coordinates with clients; attends client meetings.
  • Assists with marketing/business development; may help write proposals.
  • May serve as project manager on small projects.
  • Independently performs assignments on complex projects.
  • Coordinates assistant and associate professional staff and technical staff’s work; may supervise student or technical staff.

Olsson currently has growth opportunities for our Site Design group. This role offers flexible work options, including remote and hybrid opportunities, to accommodate diverse working preferences and promote work-life balance. Candidates can work hybrid schedules, work remotely, or work out of any Olsson office location in these regions/areas.

Applicants should have the ability to travel for in-office activities, client and site visits as needed.

  • Having ownership in the work you do.
  • Using your talents to positively affect communities.

  • Strong communication skills.
  • Ability to contribute and work well on a team.

Job Description

Vertex is seeking a Senior Program Manager to support delivery operations and execution across the Marketing Technology (MarTech) organization.

This role will partner closely with MarTech Platform Owners, Business Engagement Leads, agency partners, business stakeholders, and technology teams to coordinate delivery of marketing technology initiatives across digital experience, omnichannel engagement, customer data, content operations, and emerging AI-enabled capabilities.

The successful candidate will serve as a central coordinator for portfolio execution, helping manage integrated planning, cross-functional dependencies, delivery risks, release readiness, stakeholder communications, and operational governance activities. This individual will help ensure initiatives are delivered efficiently while improving visibility, accountability, and execution discipline across the MarTech ecosystem.

This is a hands-on contract role requiring strong program leadership, organization, communication, and stakeholder management skills within a complex, matrixed environment.

The ideal candidate will have experience working with customer engagment platforms, be strategic and organized as well have a backround in program or project management.

*** This is a 9 month contract covering a family leave ****

Key Responsibilities

Program & Delivery Management

  • Coordinate delivery of multiple concurrent MarTech initiatives across business, technology, agency, and vendor teams.
  • Develop and maintain integrated project plans, milestones, dependencies, workback schedules, decision logs, and action trackers.
  • Track delivery progress, risks, issues, assumptions, and mitigation plans; proactively escalate items requiring leadership attention.
  • Facilitate delivery status reviews and provide clear, concise execution updates to stakeholders and leadership.
  • Support execution across web and digital experience, content operations, customer engagement, marketing automation, customer data, consent and preference management, and AI-enabled capabilities.

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Serve as a central point of coordination among Platform Owners, Business Engagement Leads, business stakeholders, DCE/CIAO partners, agencies, vendors, and technology delivery teams.
  • Identify and manage dependencies across projects, platforms, teams, and release timelines.
  • Coordinate stakeholder communications and escalation pathways when scope, priorities, resources, or timelines are at risk.
  • Facilitate trade-off and decision-making discussions, documenting outcomes and driving actions to closure.
  • Support alignment with relevant Medical, Commercial, Legal, Privacy, Information Security, and other enterprise partners as required by an initiative.

Portfolio Operations & Governance Support

  • Support MarTech governance forums, portfolio reviews, planning cadences, and operational reporting.
  • Maintain portfolio views, delivery dashboards, status reports, RAID logs, capacity inputs, and other decision-support artifacts.
  • Assist with intake administration, demand tracking, impact-assessment coordination, and prioritization activities.
  • Ensure requests and initiatives are appropriately documented, routed, monitored, and progressed through established governance processes.
  • Contribute to portfolio metrics and delivery performance reporting that improve transparency, predictability, and accountability.

Launch & Release Readiness

  • Coordinate implementation readiness, testing activities, launch planning, and go-live communications across interconnected initiatives.
  • Support UAT planning, issue and defect tracking, deployment coordination, and release management activities.

  • Monitor launch dependencies and escalate readiness risks early.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to strengthen intake, governance, delivery, release, and cross-functional coordination processes.
  • Drive adoption of standardized program management practices, templates, and delivery disciplines.
  • Use automation and AI-enabled tools, where appropriate, to improve operational efficiency and reduce manual effort.
  • Contribute to scalable operating practices as the MarTech portfolio and organization continue to mature.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Systems, Marketing, Technology, Operations, or a related discipline.
  • 7+ years of experience in program management, project management, digital operations, marketing technology, or a related field.
  • Experience managing multiple concurrent initiatives in a complex, matrixed organization.
  • Experience coordinating cross-functional teams, external vendors, and agency partners.
  • Strong capability in integrated planning, dependency management, risk management, release readiness, and stakeholder communications.
  • Experience developing leadership-ready status reporting, portfolio views, and decision-support materials.
  • Demonstrated ability to bring structure to ambiguity, organize complex workstreams, and drive accountability without direct authority.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, facilitation, executive presence, and relationship-management skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting MarTech, digital transformation, customer engagement, CRM, content, web, customer data, marketing automation, or consent and preference capabilities.
  • Pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, or another highly regulated industry experience.
  • Working knowledge of Agile, hybrid delivery, and product operating models.
  • Experience with tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Smartsheet, Microsoft Project, Power BI, or comparable delivery and portfolio-management platforms.
  • Experience supporting omnichannel marketing, digital experiences, content operations, or AI-enabled marketing capabilities.

Core Competencies

Execution Leadership

Moves complex, cross-team work forward with urgency and discipline.

Portfolio Visibility

Creates clear, trusted views of status, dependencies, risks, and decisions.

Stakeholder Partnership

Builds alignment across business, technology, agencies, vendors, and governance partners.

Structured Problem Solving

Brings order to ambiguity and translates priorities into coordinated execution plans.

Influence Without Authority

Drives ownership, follow-through, and timely escalation in a matrixed environment.

Communication

Tailors concise, decision-oriented updates for delivery teams and senior stakeholders.

What Success Looks Like in the First Six Months

  • Establish reliable visibility across assigned MarTech initiatives, milestones, dependencies, risks, and decisions.
  • Improve coordination and follow-through across platform teams, stakeholders, agencies, and delivery partners.
  • Provide consistent, decision-oriented delivery reporting and governance support.
  • Drive priority initiatives forward with limited day-to-day oversight.

Ready to make a difference?

We are a relentlessly client-focused group re-imagining, re-designing, and re-engineering the way electric utilities tackle industry problems. Our transmission planning team delivers technically rigorous power system studies and strategic planning support to utilities, developers, and grid operators navigating one of the most dynamic periods in the history of the electric grid — from large-scale renewable interconnection and large load growth to FERC-driven transmission reform. We are seeking an experienced senior engineer ready to own complex engagements, lead a team, and shape the direction of our practice.

Why you will love working here:

  • Quality of life: Flexible workplace arrangements, work-life balance

  • Investment in the community: Donation matching, volunteer opportunities

  • Investment in you: Tuition reimbursement, access to professional development resources, 401k matching, Employee Stock Purchase Plan

  • And many, many more (Ask your recruiter for more details!)

The Ideal Candidate

You are a technically deep transmission planning engineer with a track record of leading complex, multi-discipline power system studies from kickoff through final deliverable. You take ownership of your work and your clients. You move fluidly between steady-state contingency analysis, transient stability, interconnection processes, and long-range buildout assessments without losing the thread. You write clearly, communicate confidently with utility decision-makers, and actively develop the engineers around you. You bring solutions, not just analyses, and you are motivated by the challenge of a grid that is changing fast.

What you will be doing:

Daily and weekly responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Serve as technical lead or study manager on transmission planning engagements, owning scope, schedule, quality, and client relationship

  • Perform steady-state load flow and contingency analysis (PSS/E, PSLF, PowerWorld) for utility transmission planning and interconnection studies

  • Conduct transient stability and dynamic simulation studies, including modeling of conventional generation and inverter-based resources (IBR)

  • Lead generation and large load interconnection impact studies, including feasibility, facilities, and cluster/serial study processes across CAISO, MISO, PJM, ERCOT, WECC, and other regional footprints

  • Develop and assess long-range transmission expansion plans evaluating load growth scenarios, generation retirement, renewable buildout, and infrastructure needs

  • Support FERC Order 1920 proactive transmission planning and Order 2023 interconnection reform compliance work for utility clients

  • Perform NERC reliability standards studies and assessments including TPL-001, FAC-001/002, TOP-001, and MOD series standards

  • Author and QA technical study reports for regulatory filings, client deliverables, and interconnection submissions

  • Develop Python-based automation and tooling to improve study execution efficiency, model management, and output quality

  • Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through technical review, guidance, and day-to-day collaboration

  • Participate in business development through proposal writing, scope development, client presentations, and identification of new opportunities

  • Monitor evolving FERC policy, regional planning standards, and grid technology trends to inform client strategy and internal capability development

What we need you to have (minimum qualifications):

  • BS in Electrical Engineering from an ABET-accredited college or university

  • 2+ years of experience in transmission planning, power system studies, or related electrical engineering

What we would like you to have:

  • Hands-on experience with PSS/E, PSLF, or equivalent transmission planning software

  • Demonstrated experience leading or managing technical study engagements as primary point of contact

  • EIT or PE registration, or active pursuit of licensure

  • Deep familiarity with regional ISOs/RTOs — including CAISO, MISO, PJM, ERCOT, WECC, SERC, NYISO, NEISO, and/or SPP — and their interconnection processes and planning criteria

  • Experience with IBR and BESS dynamic modeling under NERC MOD-026/027/031/032/033

  • Familiarity with long-range transmission expansion planning methodologies and scenario-based planning frameworks

  • Experience with large load interconnection studies for data center, hyperscaler, industrial, or other high-demand customers

  • Proficiency in Python for power system study automation, model management, and data workflows

  • Short circuit analysis experience using ASPEN, CAPE, or ETAP

  • Familiarity with electromagnetic transient software (PSCAD, EMTP) as a supplemental capability

  • Strong technical report writing skills; ability to communicate complex results clearly to non-engineering audiences and utility executives

  • Experience contributing to business development proposals and client scoping discussions

About Rimini Street, Inc.

We are actively seeking an Associate Business Analyst. This is a remote role based in Brazil.

Position Summary

This role is an Associate Business Analyst within the Global Product Delivery organization, supporting SAP and Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) solutions. The primary responsibility of this position is to assist with analyzing and translating business, tax, legal, and regulatory requirements into clear functional requirements that support compliant, high-quality ERP updates.

The Associate Business Analyst works closely with Global Tax & Regulatory, Product Management, Development, and QA teams to support requirements analysis, functional documentation, testing, and delivery activities. This role provides an opportunity to build deeper SAP or Oracle EBS expertise while contributing across the solution lifecycle, from initial research and impact assessment through testing, documentation, and deployment.

Description

TripleTen is a career learning platform for people in a world being reshaped by AI. We help people learn the tech and AI skills to move into higher-paying roles and keep up as the economy shifts. Established in 2019, we are part of Nebius Group, a global leader in AI infrastructure. We work remotely across the US, Europe, LatAm, and beyond.

About the role

﻿

Our brand and marketing team ships a lot with few people across several zones, and the small work has outgrown us: pages to update, articles to republish, tickets going stale, finished work nobody can find. This role picks that up and puts a system under it. The biggest recurring piece is the blog. Search engines were happy to leave a good article alone for a year; AI assistants are not, so everything we publish gets refreshed regularly.

You’ll report to our Brand Director and work closely with a strong team of brand, organic and social media marketers, designers, and copywriter.

What you will do

  • Blog refresh: Work closely with our SEO/GEO Growth Engineer to update roughly 10-20 published articles a month with Claude. Update facts, tighten structure, put finished text live and check if its formatting, links, images, and copy landed well.
  • Small page edits: Minor changes on live pages—a date, a price, a link. Our Claude agents know where the components live, but they need you to tell what to change.
  • Coordination: Chase the pieces an article needs before it ships: a student quote, a cover brief, a fresh instructor photo; ping a vendor for a lost invoice, get it and upload into our internal billing system.
  • The records: Keep the change log and team’s Jira board current.
  • The system: help us identify repeatable tasks and their cadence to initiate automations and then keep them running.

Requirements

  • Hands-on work with Claude or similar: You've used one on real work, and you know where it gets things wrong.
  • Junior project-management skill: You carry a batch of small tasks at once and close them without being chased. You'd rather build a system than keep remembering.
  • A careful eye: You catch a wrong number, a dead link, a changed heading.
  • B2+ English: Strong enough to spot AI patterns in published copy and hear when a sentence stops sounding natural.
  • Comfortable in a repo and a tracker: we use GitHub + Claude Code, WordPress, Jira, Figma, Notion. If you’re not familiar with them, be prepared to pick up quickly.

Nice to have:

  • Basic marketing understanding: enough context to see why a page, an article, or a funnel exists, how they get found, and question links with no UTMs.
  • Experience keeping a team's tickets, files, or documentation in order.

What we can offer you

  • Remote, part-time collaboration (about 20 hours per week).
  • Room to grow into more hours, full-time and a wider role in brand, marketing, or production.
  • Full onboarding into our AI-first stack and our brand kit.
  • A close-knit global team across the US, Europe, and LatAm.

The ideal candidate will design, develop, configure, and implement solutions to complex technical and business problems across the Security Third Party Program and the broader Security Risk Management program. jobs.description:
Workforce Classification:

Telecommuter

Join Our Team: Do Meaningful Work and Improve People’s Lives

Our purpose, to improve customers’ lives by making healthcare work better, is far from ordinary. And so are our employees. Working at Premera means you have the opportunity to drive real change by transforming healthcare.

Premera is committed to being a workplace where people feel empowered to grow, innovate, and lead with purpose. By investing in our employees and fostering a culture of collaboration and continuous development, we’re able to better serve our customers. It’s this commitment that has earned us recognition as one of the best companies to work for. Learn more about our recent awards and recognitions as a greatest workplace.

Learn how Premera supports our members, customers and the communities that we serve through our Healthsource blog: .

At Premera, we're leveraging artificial intelligence and data science to solve some of healthcare's most complex challenges and create meaningful impact for the people and communities we serve. As our Manager of AI and Data Science, you'll lead a talented team of data scientists and AI innovators developing cutting-edge solutions that improve decision-making, unlock new opportunities, and shape the future of healthcare.

We're looking for a visionary and technically strong leader who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, exploring new ideas, and turning emerging technologies into real-world results. You'll guide a high-performing team, influence strategy, collaborate across the organization, and help transform ambitious concepts into scalable AI-powered solutions that deliver measurable business value.

If you're energized by innovation, passionate about developing people, and excited to work at the intersection of AI, data science, and healthcare, we’d love to talk to you!

This is a telecommuter position, working from home.

What you’ll do:

  • Build and lead a high-performing team of data scientists, machine learning scientists, and experimental engineers, fostering a culture of innovation, rigorous experimentation, and continuous learning.

  • Stay at the forefront and capitalize on advancements in AI by driving alignment with organizational goals.

  • Leads cross-functional collaborations with business, analytical, and technical teams to ideate and develop innovative AI/ML models and actionable insights addressing complex healthcare challenges.

  • Lead hands-on exploration, development, and iterative testing of advanced AI/ML models to drive strategic insights and innovative business solutions. Champion continuous experimentation, rapid prototyping, and data-driven validation while ensuring timely, high-quality results.

  • Oversee continuous model performance monitoring to detect drift and ensure ongoing validity of AI/ML solutions. Guide re-training strategies and collaborate on timely issue resolution, maintaining scientific rigor and reliability.

  • Collaborate with stakeholders to continuously evaluate the strategic impact and business value of AI/ML prototypes and production models, ensuring that data-driven insights translate into meaningful outcomes.

  • Champion and reinforce rigorous experimentation and development best practices - including peer review, reproducible experimentation, and responsible AI principles such as fairness and explainability - to maintain high standards in all AI initiatives.

  • Mentor and coach data scientists, machine learning scientists, and experimental engineers. Foster continuous learning, advanced skill development, and professional growth in alignment with emerging AI capabilities.

  • Instill a culture of iterative experimentation and flexible, agile-like development practices, emphasizing robust documentation standards for reproducibility. Encourage continuous improvement through regular retrospectives and process enhancements that accelerate development.

  • Establish and uphold comprehensive documentation practices for experimental design, model development, and data usage, ensuring reproducibility and compliance with all CD&A and corporate standards.

  • Build strong partnerships with business leaders, fostering a deep understanding of the potential and outcomes of cutting-edge AI/ML advancements. Translate complex scientific concepts into clear, compelling narratives, ensuring stakeholders can make informed, data-driven decisions.

What you’ll bring:

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field; or 5+ years of equivalent professional experience.

  • 2+ years of experience leading highly analytical and scientific teams, guiding them through data science or machine learning.

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience developing and validating AI/ML solutions in industries with a track record of effectively transitioning models from research to pilot or POC.

  • 5+ years of experience conducting quantitative analytics.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced degree (Masters/PhD) in a quantitative, computational, or scientific field, with demonstrated expertise in AI/ML development methods.

  • 2+ years managing cross-functional research collaborations or academic/industry partnerships with a strong focus on innovative AI/ML development.

  • 5+ years expertise with core data science libraries (NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib and scikit-learn) and familiarity with advanced model interpretability libraries (e.g., SHAP, LIME) and statistical tools (e.g., Statsmodels, PyMC3).

  • Experience with NLP libraries (e.g., Hugging Face Transformers, SpaCy) or specialized packages (e.g., XGBoost, LightGBM).

  • 5+ years of experience productionizing and monitoring AI models and solutions with MLOps frameworks (e.g., MLflow, Kubeflow) for experiment tracking, model packaging, and versioning. Experience applying drift detection and continuous evaluation strategies to maintain the scientific and business relevance of AI/ML solutions.

  • 5+ years working within Agile-like test and learning environments, using iterative or sprint-based approaches to develop AI/ML proofs of concept and production-ready deliverables.

  • 5+ years of healthcare and healthcare data experience resulting in the creation of solutions and systems for the healthcare industry.

  • 2+ years implementing responsible AI practices, including model interpretability, fairness audits, and ethical risk assessments.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Experience in developing and experimenting with deep learning architectures (CNNs, transformers, LSTMs, etc.) with frameworks such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, and Keras.

  • Proven experience at building and implementing processes, controls, and methods to support the debugging of ML/AI models and enhancing predictive performance.

  • Proven experience working with ML lifecycles in experimentation contexts, including hypothesis driven development practices, rapid prototyping, and iterative model refinement.

  • Experience applying product development lifecycle methodologies to data centric products, aligning roadmaps with market or stakeholder needs and iterating on features through user feedback and data insights.

  • Prior exposure to software design patterns, microservices, distributed computing, container orchestration, and other relevant architectures.

  • Proficient in SQL for data exploration and feature engineering, with an ability to handle structured and unstructured data in various research contexts. Comfort working with evolving data formats and tools, leveraging data management best practices to support experimentation and prototyping.

  • Proven experience with a variety of statistical analyses (e.g., hypothesis testing, experimental design, regression analysis, clustering, time series analysis, anomaly detection, and sequence analysis) to data-driven decision making.

  • In-depth experience developing supervised predictive models (e.g., logistic regression, random forests, gradient boosting) and applying unsupervised learning techniques (e.g., clustering, dimensionality reduction).

  • In depth knowledge of modern deep learning models, algorithms, and architectures (self/cross attention, encoders and decoders, residual connections, normalizing layers, contrastive losses and joint embeddings, multi-task learning, transfer learning, state space models).

  • Hands-on expertise with cutting-edge generative AI techniques, including prompt engineering, various reasoning strategies, agentic frameworks, and function-calling approaches. Experience researching and prototyping innovative retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns (e.g., prompt rewriting, routing, multi-modal fusion, hierarchical navigable small world indices, reciprocal rank fusion).

  • Demonstrated expertise of prompt engineering techniques for generative AI—including role/system prompts, prompt rewrites, and context injection—to innovate in research and experimentation. Proven track record in designing and leading large-scale prompt engineering projects, optimizing prompt crafting for accuracy, interpretability, and creativity.

  • Excellent communication, collaboration, mentorship, and team leadership skills.

Physical Requirements

The following have been identified as essential physical requirements of this job and must be performed with or without an accommodation:

  • This is primarily a sedentary role which requires the ability to exert up to 10 lbs. of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects, including the human body.

  • This role requires the ability to use a keyboard and to communicate clearly and understandably in person and over the telephone.

Premera total rewards

Our comprehensive total rewards package provides support, resources, and opportunities to help employees thrive and grow. Our total rewards are more than a collection of perks, they're a reflection of our commitment to your health and well-being. We offer a broad array of rewards including physical, financial, emotional, and community benefits, including:

  • Medical, vision, and dental coverage with low employee premiums.

  • Voluntary benefit offerings, including pet insurance for paw parents.

  • Life and disability insurance.

  • Retirement programs, including a 401K employer match and, believe it or not, a pension plan that is vested after 3 years of service.

  • Wellness incentives with a wide range of mental well-being resources for you and your dependents, including counseling services, stress management programs, and mindfulness programs, just to name a few.

  • Generous paid time off to reenergize.

  • Looking for continuing education? We have tuition assistance for both undergraduate and graduate degrees.

  • Employee recognition program to celebrate anniversaries, team accomplishments, and more.

For our hybrid employees, our on-campus model provides flexibility to create your own routine with access to on-site resources, networking opportunities, and team engagement.

  • Commuter perks make your trip to work less impactful on the environment and your wallet.

  • Free convenient on-site parking.

  • Subsidized on-campus cafes make lunchtime connections with colleagues fun and affordable.

  • Participate in engaging on-site activities such as health and wellness events, coffee connects, disaster preparedness fairs and more.

  • Our complementary fitness & well-being center offers both in-person and virtual workouts and nutritional counseling.

  • Need a brain break? Challenge someone to a game of shuffleboard or ping pong while on campus.

Equal employment opportunity/affirmative action:

Premera is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. Premera seeks to attract and retain the most qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, gender or gender identity, sexual orientation, genetic information or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

We are seeking a strong Salesforce developer and Release Management Specialist for a Salesforce Digital Transformation Center (DTC). The platform includes most of Salesforce’s products including Public Sector Solutions, Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, Data360, Agentforce, Shield, Own Backup, Tableau, and Mulesoft. The DTC manages the platform and supports its tenant customer application teams.

As part of a rock star Salesforce technical team, the primary function of this role is to manage the platform and support all DTC operations to include solution consultation, design/code reviews, execution of the CI/CD process, Incident Response, and advanced system administration support activities. The candidate will also provide assistance in establishing new platform services, technology standards, security standards, and technical briefings for federal agency stakeholders.

This position requires a strong Salesforce development background, experience administering mid-to-large-sized Salesforce orgs, hands-on Git-based CI/CD performance, supporting security assessments, maintaining governance documentation, and identifying, analyzing, and managing business and technical requirements for federal government projects. The successful candidate will drive tasks to completion, is self-motivated, driven, and has experience with various Salesforce products and Docusign.

This is a client facing role where a developer-level knowledge of the Salesforce platform is expected, including familiarity with core platform capabilities, common system/user administration tasks, system integrations, programmatic (code) and declarative (no-code) configuration mechanics. jobs.title: Content Writer (Remote, £31-33k)
jobs.excerpt: Ellipsis is emerging as a market leader in “GEO” for B2B technology companies.
jobs.description:
Ellipsis is emerging as a market leader in “GEO” for B2B technology companies. This is a high-impact, varied role in a fast-moving and ambitious agency.

The transition to AI search has put a lot of the SEO industry on the back foot. Ellipsis has always been consultative/strategic in our approach; we started building AI search products in 2021 on GPT-2, and thus this has been a time for us to thrive.

Today, we think we have a better understanding of AI search than almost anyone else. We have both the tracking product (built in-house), the data (~25 million AI answers for analysis, with more tracked weekly), and the execution end-to-end from strategy, to writing, to in-house design, to optimization, and performance reporting.

As the newest member of our in-house Writing team, you will craft outstanding content for our clients that uses – and feeds into – our latest AI search research. Content quality is extremely important to us! For the writer who can think strategically, learn quickly, and execute across a variety of subject matters (typically SaaS/tech), this is the dream role.

What you’ll do

The heart of this role is the content creation itself -- taking a brief and working with a combination of your own skill and our cutting-edge AI tooling to turn it into a genuinely good piece of content. You’ll work on a varied mix of content for your assigned portfolio of clients, including (but not limited to) landing pages, informational content, comparison pieces, and listicles.

Every article we produce needs to win the trust of readers, capture the voice of the brand, and be built to perform in both AI Search (GEO) and legacy search. You don’t need to be an expert in GEO from day one, but you’ll need a genuine interest in how it works and the ability to learn quickly, because it shapes how we build every content piece.

Ellipsis uses AI in the writing process, and we produce a high volume of content. Ellipsis is also extremely anti-slop! Your job as a writer will be to use our custom AI tooling and craft high-quality and strategically impactful work that leverages Ellipsis’ very latest research on how AI search actually works. We are continually improving our processes and tooling, and you will be expected to feed back on what works (and what doesn’t) so we can get better faster.

To succeed in this role, you need to be comfortable with leveraging AI for the parts of the writing process it’s great at, then build on top of this. AI handles the groundwork; your judgment and skill is what lifts the output above what any tool produces on its own. You’ll still have plenty of room for craft and creativity -- deciding what’s actually good is the part we can’t automate.

Communication, both with clients and the wider team, is also a core part of the role. You will be joining a small but growing team of four writers, and will work closely with our Content, Strategy, and Design teams. While you won’t own or manage client relationships directly, nor will you attend every check-in call, deeply understanding your clients’ products, audiences, and goals will be critical to creating effective content. You’ll need to be confident in gathering the information you need from clients and the internal team through onboarding calls, check-ins, and asynchronous communication.

Our customers are predominantly B2B technology companies. We work with a lot of startups and scale-ups; B2B tech has been our bread-and-butter although we are also having success with B2C and have some very high profile clients in this area. The range of topics you’ll work on will be wide, and you’ll thus need to be confident with context switching and picking up varying styles and requirements across different clients quickly.

As a 100% remote team, we carefully balance collaboration with an environment that enables everyone to do their best work. You’ll communicate with the team through Basecamp, our project management software, and Google Meet. The majority of the team is located in Europe, and you’ll be expected to regularly attend meetings between 10am–3pm GMT, with occasional calls outside these times.

Requirements

We’re looking for an experienced writer who can work well both independently and as part of a team. We’d expect at least 2-4 years of writing and editing experience. Excellent writing and grammar, and the discipline to fact-check every stat, price, and claim against primary sources are hard requirements.

You’ll need to be confident in getting up to speed fast on unfamiliar B2B and SaaS topics and turn them into compelling, user-friendly content. A working understanding of GEO would be an advantage, but what we’re really looking for is somebody with an eagerness to learn and the ability to do so quickly.

Strong critical thinking is a must-have at Ellipsis! You’ll need to be confident weighing sources, questioning a brief that doesn’t add up, and making sound editorial judgement calls without constant guidance. We are looking for writers who can spot gaps or friction within our current processes and systems, and help drive forward improvements.

The ideal candidate will also be able to demonstrate the following soft skills:

  • Proven organisational skills: You must be obsessive with deadlines, managing and updating tasks, and totally reliable.
  • Fantastic communication skills: Remote work relies on mutual trust, so frequent and clear written communication is essential.
  • Receptive to feedback with no ego and solutions-oriented: You can take an edit or a critique, act on it, and get better. At Ellipsis, continuous improvement is more important than being right.
  • High level of self-awareness, a “people person”: You’ll be dealing with members of the team on a daily basis, so this is an integral part of the role.
  • Self-driven work ethic: You need to be self-motivated, comfortable taking the initiative, and see projects through to completion.

Benefits

  • This is a full-time, 100% remote role. You’ll be a full team member, and involved in our team projects, work, and meetups.
  • £31-33k/year salary, depending on experience, with pension benchmarked to UK rates.
  • 28 days of paid holiday, with an additional 1 paid holiday day a year with each year of tenure, up to a maximum of 5 additional days.
  • 4-day work week, once a month.
  • Genuinely flexible working.
  • Regular team retreats (~1 per year); last was Istanbul, previously in Edinburgh, Oxford, Madrid, and Budapest.
  • Time and budget for learning and development.
  • Enhanced maternity/paternity leave, and sick pay.

Application process

It’s important we find the best candidate for this position, and our selection process will reflect this. You’ll be required to attend at least three interviews (by video call) and carry out a (paid) freelance project with us before we make an employment offer.

Much of our company Wiki is externally accessible, and you’re encouraged to read through this before applying. We have a very useful guide to our interview process available here. This tells you what we’re looking for and reading this will significantly increase your chance of success!

Please apply through Workable: . We will decide who progresses to the next stage based on the form you submit, your cover letter, and your CV. Please give us a good reason to select you! Taking the time to research the role, what we’re looking for, what we do, and what you can do for us will increase your chance of success. Your cover letter is where you have the space to do this.

Whilst we love technology and sit at the leading edge of its adoption (we automate hundreds of thousands of actions a month internally), we want to hear from you rather than from ChatGPT. That might sound odd given how much AI is in the work itself -- so to be clear: we use AI heavily day to day, but your application is where we want to see how you think, in your own words.

The deadline for submission is the end of the day, on 30th September 2026. We’ll be in touch with all candidates following the close of applications.

We do great work for clients and are building an ethical business that lets everyone do their best work. If you think you could be the next person to join our team, please apply!

jobs.description:
Job Description

At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.

Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale.

The Safety Assurance for Effective Autonomous Driving Software (SAFE-ADS) department is part of GM’s Global Product Safety, System, and Certification organization. Our mission is to help GM deliver trustworthy automated-driving products.

As the central authority for automated-driving system safety, the department brings together experts from across the company to develop and maintain a comprehensive safety case, including safety performance indicators for GM’s automated-driving technologies. GM’s vision is zero crashes, zero emissions, and zero congestion, and autonomous vehicle safety is essential to achieving that vision.

The Role

The AV Safety Engineering Analytics team is seeking an experienced Safety Data Analysis Engineer to provide engineering support for AV Operational Safety and Issue Response. This is a safety engineering role focused on data-driven issueresponse and investigation. You will combine engineering judgment, safety analysis, and strong data skills to investigate potential issues, organize event-related data, and develop evidence that supports AV Safety Assurance and AV Operational Safety decisions.

The role is designed for an engineer who is highly proficient in navigating, integrating, designing, and analyzing large-scale data. You will support rapid, highly iterative investigations involving specific vehicles, locations, software releases, event sequences, operational conditions, and other issue-relevant dimensions.

The scale of AV operations, including potential issues, actual events, readiness drills, and ongoing software releases, creates a need for rapid, detailed, event-driven analyses. At the same time, you will help convert repeatable investigation patterns into reusable analytics and issue-detection methods.

What You'll Do

  • Respond collaboratively to AV Safety Strategy and Assurance and AV Operations requests for potential issue-specific analyses, event-related data organization, and root-cause investigations.

  • Collaborate with Engineering, Operations, and Safety teams to investigate potentialAV issues and conduct root-cause analyses.

  • Translate investigation needs into clear analysis requirements, data requirements, analytical designs, and execution plans in collaboration with requesting teams.

  • Establish and support rapid incident-response and targeted-analysis capabilities that leverage standing data pipelines as well as unique issue- and incident-relevant data sources.

  • Integrate vehicle telemetry, time-series signals, event and incident records, readiness-drill data, software-release information, location and operational context, and other relevant sources into analysis-ready datasets.

  • Distinguish data-quality, sensor, instrumentation, and pipeline issues from meaningful operational outliers using engineering judgment and data validation methods.

  • Deliver concise, technically rigorous analysis findings, readouts, and evidence that help partner teams assess potential operations safety issues and determine appropriate next steps.

  • Identifyinvestigation workflows that can be generalized into reusable metrics, detection methods, pipelines, or analysis tooling without losing the flexibility required for issue investigation.

  • Apply engineering and physics-based methods, including signal decomposition, filtering, smoothing, sampling, and feature construction, to transform noisy signals into physically meaningful representations of vehicle behavior and system performance.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, physics, applied mathematics, or a related physical science.

  • 5+ years of relevant professional experience analyzing large-scale time-series, telemetry, vehicle, robotics, or other engineering data, including working with Robot Operating System (ROS) logs.

  • Strong working knowledge of Python and SQL.

  • Experience with time-series analysis, including signal decomposition, filtering, smoothing, sampling, feature construction, or related signal-processing methods.

  • Experience designing and executing ad hoc analyses while recognizing opportunities to develop scalable, repeatable analytical methods.

  • Experience gathering analytical requirements, defining data needs, selecting appropriate methods, and communicating findings to partner teams.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work effectively in fast-moving, ambiguous, and highly iterative investigations.

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to craft fact-based reports through individual and collaborative work across safety, operations, human factors, data engineering, and emerging-issues teams.

What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Experience in autonomous vehicles, advanced driver-assistance systems, robotics, transportation safety, or a related domain.

  • Experience performing AV- or SDV-specific issue detection, anomaly detection, event investigation, or root-cause analysis.

  • Experience analyzing large-scale vehicle motion, driving context, automated-driving performance, or operational data.

  • Experience developing safety performance indicators, safety monitoring methods, or evidence used in safety assurance and operations decisions.

  • Experience working with cloud-based data platforms, distributed processing, or large-scale analytics workflows.

  • Experience with BigQuery or comparable cloud data platforms.

  • Familiarity with C++ or C++-based robotics and vehicle software environments.

  • Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, GitHub, CI/CD, version control, or related software-development workflows.

  • Experience collaborating with human-factors, operations, systems, validation, verification, or safety-assurance teams.

  • Publications, conference participation, or other demonstrated engagement in vehicle safety, robotics safety, safety analytics, or related technical work.

This role will serve as a PFML subject matter expert and will be responsible for helping design and build the future-state PFML claims operation. The PFML Claims Consultant will partner closely with Product, Technology, Legal, Compliance, and Operations teams to define business requirements, support system configuration and testing, develop workflows, create claims procedures and training materials, drive process improvements, and ensure regulatory requirements are effectively translated into scalable operational solutions. The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise, regulatory knowledge, critical thinking, and compassion while helping customers navigate important life events.

  • Experience interpreting statutes, regulations, policy provisions, administrative guidelines, and complex business requirements.

jobs.title: Senior Communications Officer, Strategic Communications
jobs.excerpt: GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good.
jobs.description:
GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good. Our work, which focuses on global health and well-being, is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025. We anticipate our total grantmaking is likely to approach or even exceed $1 billion this year, and we are working toward a future that could be several times that scale. Through years of deliberate groundwork, we’ve been growing our research capacity and scope in order to direct substantially more funding to the most impactful opportunities we can find.

We’re hiring a Senior Communications Officer, Strategic Communications to lead GiveWell’s development of messaging and narratives that explain its work across different audiences and contexts. You will translate the organization’s increasingly diverse and complex work into clear, accurate communications and lead major initiatives that require close coordination across GiveWell.

This role reports to Steven Profaizer, our Vice President of Communications, and will lead a small and growing team. This is one of three new communications leadership roles, alongside a Senior Communications Officer, Media & Public Affairs and a Senior Communications Officer, Editorial & Production.

About the role

Both our research and impact are expanding. Last year, we directed more than $400 million to highly cost-effective programs that save and improve lives. This year, we expect our grantmaking to approach, and possibly exceed, $1 billion.

To build toward the communications capacity this next stage requires, we are rapidly expanding our team. Together with the Vice President of Communications, the three new Senior Communications Officers will form GiveWell’s communications leadership team. Each leader will own their function, but much of the work that matters most—like team strategies, major initiatives, partnership campaigns, and how we present the organization as a whole—will involve all three. We will expect this group to set shared priorities and work closely together to achieve the team’s goals.

In this hands-on leadership position, you’ll own how GiveWell explains its work across different audiences and contexts, with end-to-end responsibility for this emerging function. You’ll set its strategy, hire and develop its people, build its systems, and personally own its hardest and most consequential work. This is an opportunity to build, not just inherit, an important function at a critical point in GiveWell’s development. You’ll start with a small team and grow it over time.

While this role is set at the Senior Communications Officer level, we may consider hiring an exceptional candidate as a Communications Director—with greater expectations, responsibilities, and compensation.

What You'll Do

As Senior Communications Officer, Strategic Communications, you will be responsible for translating GiveWell’s research, grantmaking, and ideas into messages, frameworks, and products across a variety of channels and contexts. You will also lead major communications initiatives, advise senior leaders and teams, and help GiveWell assess and respond to emerging communications opportunities and risks.

Specific duties will include:

  • Own how GiveWell’s brand positioning and guidelines are applied across teams, channels, and partnership communications, and work closely with the Vice President of Communications on developing and maintaining them.
  • Own the messaging and narrative that make GiveWell’s work accessible and relevant without sacrificing rigor, precision, or clarity about uncertainty.
  • Translate GiveWell’s research, grantmaking, and ideas into messages and frameworks tailored to the audiences we most need to reach.
  • Partner with Philanthropy on GiveWell’s donor communications strategy and lead donor-facing communications that require new or tailored messaging.
  • Lead complex, cross-functional communications initiatives, including major partnership campaigns and other high-priority communications involving grantees and external partners.
  • Serve as a strategic communications advisor to senior leaders and teams across GiveWell, bringing a clear point of view on audiences, framing, opportunities, and risks.
  • Lead GiveWell’s internal assessment of emerging issues that may affect the organization and develop our position and messaging, working with relevant teams and the Senior Communications Officer, Media & Public Affairs.
  • Own the strategic direction and institutional messaging for GiveWell’s website, working with communications colleagues on execution.
  • Own GiveWell’s internal communications strategy and major internal communications, helping our growing organization stay informed and aligned.
  • Manage and develop one or two team members initially, and help determine how the function’s team, systems, and capabilities should grow over time.

About You

You are skilled at using communications to help people understand complex ideas, build trust, and take action. You are comfortable being accountable for outcomes, making consequential decisions with limited oversight, and knowing which decisions genuinely require escalation.

You are energized by intellectually demanding work, and the challenges of creating engaging communications within a careful and precise style. You can engage deeply with GiveWell’s research, and you are comfortable understanding and communicating about data in detail. You have a long track record of getting up to speed quickly on complex subject matter and carefully communicating to a very high standard. You can build a compelling narrative that is entirely factual, representing what is known and unknown without overstating or hedging into vagueness—and you find the idea of working with GiveWell’s exacting communications standards exciting rather than limiting.

Your background includes significant experience leading communications in complex, high-stakes environments. This should include 10+ years of experience developing institutional narratives and messaging, advising senior leaders, communicating complex or technical material, and leading cross-functional initiatives. You have deep experience owning that work end to end, not just contributing to it. You’ve remained a hands-on leader who enjoys the work itself, as well as the strategy and systems behind it.

You can assess a situation from multiple angles, determine what an organization should say and how it should frame the issue, and turn that judgment into messages and communications that others can use. Experience with organizational positioning, brand strategy, donor communications, web strategy, and internal communications is desired, but we do not expect every candidate to have worked extensively in all of these areas.

In addition to demonstrated expertise in the duties listed above, you should have:

  • Exceptional communications judgment, including the ability to understand audience, context, risk, timing, and the underlying substance of a message.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to quickly make complex ideas clear and compelling without sacrificing rigor or nuance.
  • A track record of building and leading: you have created or substantially rebuilt a team or function—not only run ones you inherited—and you have hired, developed, and managed people.
  • Recent, hands-on excellence at your craft: you can point to work from the past few years that you personally produced or substantially shaped.
  • Experience producing communications that are direct and factual while being engaging and effective with their target audiences—work that succeeds through substance and clarity rather than embellishment.
  • Intellectual curiosity and the ability to engage deeply with GiveWell’s research and ideas, even without prior experience in our giving areas.
  • Experience advising executives or other senior decision-makers directly.
  • Strong alignment with GiveWell’s mission and values, including truth-seeking, transparency, and a commitment to communicating accurately and thoughtfully.

We also think these qualities will help you do well in the role and at GiveWell:

  • People who can develop a strong point of view and hold it with confidence, but remain genuinely open to challenge, new information, and better ideas.
  • Self-starters who take ownership, are comfortable creating structure in an evolving environment, and can make thoughtful decisions without always having complete information.
  • People who are proactive and anticipatory, who identify opportunities, risks, bottlenecks, and communications needs before they become obvious.
  • Collaborative leaders who raise the quality of the work around them and build strong relationships across teams.
  • People who coordinate well with peers, resolve dependencies and disagreements, and make shared work clearer rather than more complicated.

Key Questions & Information

What are some of the reasons I might not like this role?

  • You want to step into a mature function with established systems, rather than build one while you run it.
  • You do best with clear direction and established priorities. We’ll expect you to set most of your own, make most decisions yourself, and reach substantial autonomy within your first six months.
  • You prefer advising on communications to producing and being accountable for them.
  • You want sole ownership of an organization’s overarching communications strategy and brand. At GiveWell, the Vice President of Communications owns that direction; you would help shape it and lead your function within it.
  • You want to lead a large team from day one. This team is small today, and much of the most difficult work will be yours to do directly.
  • You find standards of precision and understatement limiting and frustrating. We work extremely hard to only communicate accurately what we know and what we don’t.

Can I apply to more than one of the Senior Communications Officer roles?

You can, but most people shouldn’t. We’re looking for deep expertise in these areas, and we expect most candidates with required expertise will be a clear fit for a single role. If you’re one of the few with real depth in more than one area, apply to both and tell us why. Otherwise, apply for the role you are most qualified for, and we’ll let you know if we think another role might suit you better.

What does this interview process entail?

We’ll use a combination of interviews, written exercises, and work trials to assess the qualities described above. We’ll share more specific details if we invite you to move forward to any of the following stages, but our current plan is:

  • Application
  • Interview with a member of the Talent Acquisition Team
  • Compensated, ~4-hour work trial
  • Interview with the Vice President of Communications
  • Values interview
  • Compensated, ~4-hour work trial with the Vice President of Communications
  • CEO interview and References

Note that you don’t need to submit a cover letter. We rely heavily on your resume and answers to the application questions below when we’re making early decisions. We encourage you to spend time responding to the application questions thoroughly and carefully.

Details

  • Team: You’ll report to our Vice President of Communications, collaborate closely with the two other Senior Communications Officers, and lead a small team that you’ll develop over time.
  • Compensation: This role is set at the Senior Communications Officer level. For an exceptional candidate, we may consider hiring at the Communications Director level—with greater expectations, responsibilities, and compensation.
    • NYC or the San Francisco Bay Area: $250,000
    • All other U.S. locations: $225,000
    • International: Custom based on location. We can give you a specific number at the penultimate stage of the hiring process.
  • Location: GiveWell’s staff work primarily remotely within the U.S. and abroad.
    • Offices: You are welcome but not required to work from our offices in Oakland, California, or Brooklyn, NYC.
    • International work: We are happy to employ staff internationally on a case-by-case basis. Given the managerial nature of this role, a successful candidate will need to work hours that have a certain minimum overlap with American working hours and the schedules of key coworkers.
  • Flexibility: We support and encourage flexible working, including flexible hours, working remotely, and working from the office when you choose. The majority of our staff, including senior management, work flexibly in one way or another.
  • Visa Sponsorship: If you want to work in the United States and need a work visa, we’ll do our best to sponsor it (and also cover up to 100% of relocation expenses on a case-by-case basis). Please note that government entities ultimately dictate our ability to sponsor visas.
  • Benefits: Our benefits include:
    • Fully funded health, dental, vision, and life insurance (we cover 100% of premiums within the US for you and any dependents)
    • Four weeks of paid time off per year
    • 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave
    • Ergonomic home workstations or coworking space memberships
    • 403(b) retirement plan
  • Travel: Communications staff members should expect to attend three week-long retreats each year to bond with other team members and complete in-person work. Other domestic and international travel may be required, but isn’t expected to be a regular part of these roles. We’ll discuss travel obligations in more detail during late stages of the hiring process, and we’ll give reasonable consideration to staff who have family or other obligations.
  • Start date: We’d like a candidate to start as soon as possible after receiving an offer, but we’ll offer flexibility for candidates whose personal or professional circumstances require them to moderately delay their start date.

About GiveWell

GiveWell is dedicated to finding and evaluating highly cost-effective global health and development opportunities, and we publish all the work, reasoning, and uncertainties behind our funding decisions. Our giving funds enable donors to contribute to the most impactful and cost-effective programs our researchers identify.

GiveWell is one of the world’s largest private funders of global development efforts. Trusted annually by tens of thousands of donors, GiveWell searches for highly cost-effective programs that save or improve lives the most. Since 2007, more than 150,000 donors have given over $2.6 billion through GiveWell to the most promising programs its research has identified, which we estimate will save more than 340,000 lives.

GiveWell is most well-known for recommending a small number of Top Charities, which currently support seasonal malaria chemoprevention, insecticide-treated nets, vaccine incentivization, and vitamin A supplementation. However, most of our research capacity and grantmaking is devoted to cost-effective opportunities outside of those programs.

GiveWell grants have:

  • Helped governments navigate changes to the funding landscape and implement high-impact health programs, like HIV/syphilis screening and treatment for pregnant people in Zambia and Cameroon.
  • Sought to scope and scale promising interventions that don’t have clear existing implementers. We are supporting the Clinton Health Access Initiative’s Incubator to identify potentially cost-effective interventions and create programs that we would be excited to support in the future. For example, we funded a program to prevent tuberculosis among young children in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, India, that we co-designed with CHAI through the Incubator program.
  • Provided funding to ensure that programs that recently faced foreign aid funding cuts could continue, like healthcare support and malnutrition treatment in northern Cameroon.
  • Funded program delivery alongside strengthened monitoring and evaluation, as in our grants to support treatment of clubfoot and to evaluate the program.
  • Tested our assumptions and refined our understanding through further research and data collection, including improved estimates of disease burden and studies on the effect of water chlorination on mortality and the impact of a tree-planting program on farmers’ income.

We make our reasoning public and transparent so others can challenge it (sometimes we even pay people to point out our errors). We go to unusual lengths to check our assumptions and assess our impact, including funding research to address our uncertainties and gathering independent monitoring and evaluation data about the programs we support. We change our minds when the evidence demands it. For more about GiveWell, listen to Ezra Klein’s recent interview with GiveWell’s co-founder and CEO Elie Hassenfeld.

Additional information

We don’t want to miss candidates that could do great things at GiveWell. Practically, that means a GiveWell staff member reviews every application carefully, considering the whole picture of your background and potential. If you’re on the fence about applying because you meet some but not 100% of our preferred qualifications (some studies suggest this hesitation is especially common for women and people of color), we encourage you to apply anyway.

The project manager role serves as a lead project manager for the team, ensuring successful project deliverables and completion for complex and high-priority projects that may span across multiple teams.   • Documents all project deliverables and maintains comprehensive records including correspondence, design plans, and other project related files.
  • Mentors staff within the team on project management best practices utilizing Olsson Project Management programs and other project support services resources.

Candidates can work hybrid schedules, work remotely, or work out of any Olsson office location in these regions/areas.

Olsson specializes in engineering and design, client advisory services, planning, field services, and environmental. Improving the world has been our mindset from the very beginning, back when Olsson first opened for business in 1956. And it will be our mindset for years to come.

Adventist HealthCare seeks to hire an experienced Clinical Documentation Integrity Quality Reviewer for our Clinical Documentation department who will embrace our mission to extend God’s care through the ministry of physical, mental, and spiritual healing.

• Collaborate with CDI leadership to recommend quality improvement initiatives, update audit tools, refine CDI workflows, and ensure all documentation aligns with regulatory requirements, such as CMS guidelines, HIPAA, and organizational policies.
• Analyze findings, identify trends in documentation and coding practices, and provide detailed feedback to CDI team members to support professional development.

• Doctor of Medicine (MD), Doctor of Osteopathy (DO), Foreign Medical Graduate (FMG), or Registered Nurse (RN)

You’ll work cross-functionally with other Marketing teams, Data, Engineering, Product and Finance teams to improve our performance

Qualifications
